text: The Dual Certificate Program in Generative AI and Agentic AI Development teaches prompt engineering, RAG, agent frameworks, production deployment, and domain use cases through weekend live sessions.
The program runs on Saturdays and Sundays. Each teaching session combines theory and practical work in a three-hour classroom or live-stream format.
The Retrieval-Augmented Generation module teaches embeddings, vector stores, retrieval, generation, multimodal retrieval, and evaluation for real-world knowledge assistants.
Vector Search 101 introduces embeddings, cosine similarity, dense retrieval, sparse retrieval, FAISS, and the cost of embedding documents.
The Text-RAG Pipeline practical connects chunking, retrieval, generation, and retrieval evaluation using a document corpus and a vector store.
Refund requests are reviewed according to the enrollment agreement. Processing timelines depend on payment method and approval status.
Once course access and learning materials have been activated, refunds may be restricted depending on the applicable batch and enrollment terms.
Installment plans must be cleared according to the confirmed payment schedule. Missed payments can temporarily affect access to learning resources.
Career support includes resume guidance, mock interviews, portfolio review, and placement drive coordination through the career enhancement cell.
A strong AI portfolio should show a working application, clean code, a short demo video, a README, and a clear explanation of business value.
Internal placement partner notes should not be shared publicly. Trainers may discuss general career preparation but must not disclose partner-specific hiring pipelines.
DoubtBusters are weekly support sessions for specific academic doubts. Learners should submit precise questions through the Campus Connect portal before attending.
Campus Connect provides access to learning materials, session recordings, support tickets, DoubtBuster forms, and communication from the academic team.
Attendance is tracked for live sessions. Learners who miss class should review recordings and raise specific doubts through the approved support channels.
Chroma is useful for local prototyping because it can persist collections on disk and lets a Python application reload indexed documents without re-embedding them.
Pinecone is useful when a team wants managed vector infrastructure, namespaces, serverless scaling, metadata filtering, and cloud-hosted production retrieval.
Weaviate is useful when teams want an open-source vector database with strong hybrid search features that combine semantic vector matching with BM25 keyword retrieval.
Metadata filtering improves retrieval by restricting candidate documents by source, department, date, tenant, permission level, or document type before ranking results.
Namespaces partition records inside a vector index. They are commonly used to isolate tenants, environments, regions, or data domains without creating many separate indexes.
A RAG system must never retrieve confidential records for a public query. Access level should be enforced as metadata filtering before the model receives context.

The legacy AI course brochure describes a six-month track with outdated tooling and does not reflect the current Generative AI and Agentic AI curriculum.
Production RAG systems should avoid placing personally identifiable information in prompts unless there is a clear business need, access control, and audit trail.
AI applications should track embedding cost, generation cost, latency, cache hit rate, and retrieval quality to avoid silent production drift.
The program is suitable for CS and IT graduates, working engineers, data professionals, and managers who want structured hands-on exposure to GenAI systems.
Basic Python familiarity is helpful. Learners do not need prior production AI experience because the course starts with foundations and builds toward deployment.
Before the vector database lab, trainers should verify the OpenAI key, create the class virtual environment, run the offline checks, and run the Python demo once to confirm collection creation.
Production vector database selection should consider persistence, metadata filtering, hybrid retrieval, access control, update frequency, monitoring, backup strategy, and cost.
Old Pinecone examples may import pinecone-client and pinecone.init. Newer projects should use the pinecone package and the current Pinecone client style.

Queries must be embedded with the same model that embedded the stored documents. Changing the embedding model, such as text-embedding-3-small to text-embedding-3-large, changes vector dimensions and meaning, so the persisted collection must be re-embedded and rebuilt.
